items.title: Travel insurance guidance for the United Arab Emirates
items.body_md:
For the UAE, make sure your travel insurance includes cover for private medical treatment costs and emergency medical evacuation. Healthcare facilities are of a similar standard to the UK, but you may be refused treatment or face high bills if you cannot show insurance or means to pay. The emergency medical number is 998 for an ambulance.

Keep your insurance policy details and the emergency number 998 with you at all times. If you have a health condition or are pregnant, check that your policy covers related care and possible evacuation before you travel.

After a medical incident, call 998 first if it is urgent. Then contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as you can, and keep all medical reports, receipts and proof of payment to support any claim.
claim_checklist: Call 998 for an ambulance in a medical emergency.
Contact your travel insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Keep all medical reports, receipts and proof of payment.
Follow your insurer's instructions before agreeing to non-emergency treatment if possible.
Obtain a written medical report from the treating facility if you can.
Submit your claim with the required documents within the insurer's time limit.

items.title: Travel insurance essentials for Albania
items.body_md:
Medical care in Albania is generally paid out of pocket by visitors; there is no reciprocal free healthcare agreement for Australians, and standards, equipment, medicines, and specialist access can be limited, especially outside Tirana. Travel medical insurance that covers hospital stays, treatment, and emergency medical evacuation is important because evacuation can be very expensive.

Ambulance services are limited; in some cases you may need to take a taxi or private vehicle to a hospital. Keep your policy certificate, emergency assistance phone number, and ID with you, and know how to contact your insurer's 24/7 assistance line.

After an incident, contact your insurer or assistance provider as soon as it is safe, get receipts and medical reports, and check your policy wording for coverage limits, exclusions, planned activities, and evacuation terms.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Tell them where you are, what happened, and the treatment or transport needed.
Keep receipts, invoices, medical reports, and any police reports.
Get written documentation from the hospital or clinic, including diagnosis and treatment.
If you need evacuation, get insurer approval before arranging transport where possible.
Submit your claim using the insurer's required forms and copies of all documents.
Follow up in writing and keep a record of dates and names.

items.title: Travel insurance basics for Argentina
items.body_md:
Good health care is available in Buenos Aires but may be limited elsewhere in Argentina. Hospital physicians often expect immediate cash payment for medical care, so make sure you have access to sufficient funds and arrange cover for medical treatment, hospital stays and medical evacuation. Some medicines may not be available locally, so check your needs before travel.

Sources differ on whether insurance is required for entry: one travel source says Argentina mandates valid travel medical insurance for non-resident foreign tourists as of July 2025, while others describe it as not required. In practice, cover for medical emergencies, evacuation and repatriation, lost baggage and trip disruption is widely advised. Adventure activities, caving or remote travel may need extra cover, so check the policy wording.

Keep your policy number, insurer emergency contact and the emergency numbers 107 or 911 with you. If you are referred to a medical facility, contact your insurance or medical assistance company quickly. After an incident, save all receipts, reports and medical notes, and ask your insurer how to submit a claim.
claim_checklist: Call 107 or 911 and ask for an ambulance in a medical emergency.
Contact your insurer or medical assistance company promptly if you are referred to a medical facility.
Keep all receipts, invoices and medical or incident reports.
Ask the hospital or clinic for an itemised bill and any medical notes before you leave.
Submit your claim using the forms and documents your insurer asks for.
Keep copies of everything you send and note who you spoke to and when.

items.title: Travel Insurance Guidance for Austria
items.body_md:
When travelling to Austria, make sure your travel insurance covers medical treatment costs. Medical care in Austria is not free, and public hospitals often require payment up front before providing care or admitting a patient. U.S. Medicare, Medicaid, and many U.S. health plans do not cover expenses abroad, and most Austrian hospitals and doctors do not accept U.S. health insurance.

It is particularly important to include coverage for medical evacuation and hospital stays. Healthcare facilities are excellent and available throughout the country, but evacuation can be costly if you need to be moved for treatment. Even for short visits, the U.S. Department of State strongly recommends a plan that covers medical evacuation.

Keep your insurance policy details, emergency assistance contact number, and any claim forms with you during your trip. After any medical incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible, save all receipts and medical reports, and ask your insurer about the specific steps for your policy.
claim_checklist: Notify your insurer or their emergency assistance line as soon as possible after the incident.
Keep all original receipts, invoices, and medical reports from the hospital or doctor.
Ask the healthcare provider for a written itemised bill and any diagnosis or treatment notes.
Take photos of documents if originals cannot be kept.
Complete the insurer's claim form and attach all required documentation.
Submit the claim following your policy's instructions and deadlines.
Follow up with the insurer if you do not receive confirmation or a decision.

items.title: Australia: travel insurance essentials
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for Australia should cover medical treatment and hospital stays, because healthcare is excellent but payment is generally expected at the time of service. U.S. Medicare and Medicaid do not apply, and most Australian hospitals and doctors do not accept U.S. health insurance directly; public facilities may still charge visitors unless a reciprocal arrangement applies to your nationality. Check whether your country has a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia, and carry your passport and, if relevant, your Medicare card to prove eligibility.

Include cover for medical evacuation and unexpected local treatment, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant. Emergency medical help is available by dialling 000 and asking for an ambulance. If you plan outdoor activities, follow safety advice such as staying on marked trails and not trekking alone, and check your policy wording to confirm the activity is covered.

Always keep your insurance details and emergency contact numbers with you. After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible, save receipts and documentation, and ask the insurer what they need to process a claim.
claim_checklist: Call 000 for emergency medical help if needed.
Contact your insurer as soon as reasonably possible.
Keep all medical reports, receipts, and proof of payment.
Note dates, locations, and names of any provider or facility.
Ask your insurer for the exact claim forms and required documents.
Check your policy wording for time limits and exclusions before submitting.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Belgium
items.body_md:
Belgium requires some visitors to show proof of travel health insurance that covers emergency medical care and medical evacuation, valid throughout the Schengen States for the stay, with minimum coverage of 30,000 euros. Check your policy wording to confirm it meets this requirement before you travel.

Medical care standards are high, but non-emergency consultations and prescriptions can involve fees, and unexpected treatment or evacuation may be costly. Travel insurance can help cover local treatment, hospital stays, and emergency medical evacuation, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant.

In an emergency, call 112 and ask for an ambulance. Keep all medical records, receipts, and any police or incident reports; you may be able to recover eligible costs through your travel insurance. Ask your insurer what documents they need and confirm what your policy covers.
claim_checklist: Call 112 for an ambulance in a medical emergency and get treatment as needed.
Keep all medical reports, prescriptions, receipts, and proof of payment.
Note dates, providers, and a short description of what happened.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible and ask what forms or documents are required.
Check your policy wording for deadlines, exclusions, and required proof.
Submit your claim with the requested documents and copies of receipts.
Follow up with the insurer if you do not receive confirmation or a decision.

items.title: Brazil travel insurance: key cover and claims steps
items.body_md:
Travel insurance is not legally required to enter Brazil, but it is strongly recommended because medical care for international visitors can be costly, and public hospitals may have limited English-speaking staff or lack specialised care in rural areas. Look for a policy with solid emergency medical coverage and medical evacuation, as U.S. health insurance and Medicare are generally not accepted.

Private hospitals in urban centres can offer good care but may charge high fees, while many providers only accept cash payments. In an emergency, call 192 and ask for an ambulance. Contact your insurance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility for treatment.

Before you buy, check the policy wording to confirm it covers the activities you plan, any health conditions you have, and unexpected medical evacuation. Keep your policy details with you and save all receipts and medical reports.
claim_checklist: Call 192 for an ambulance in a medical emergency
Contact your insurance company quickly if referred to a medical facility
Keep all receipts, invoices, and proof of payment, as many providers accept cash only
Ask for written medical reports and itemised bills
Check your policy wording for notification deadlines and covered activities
Submit the claim with the documents your insurer requests

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Canada
items.body_md:
Medical treatment in Canada can be very expensive, and there are no special arrangements for British visitors. Your travel insurance should cover emergency medical treatment, hospital stays, and unexpected medical evacuation. This is particularly important if you have a health condition or are pregnant.

If your trip includes remote or wilderness areas, check that your policy includes emergency evacuation and repatriation, as access to medical care can be difficult and costly. Make sure you understand any exclusions for activities you plan to do.

Keep your policy details and the insurer's 24-hour emergency contact number with you, along with the local emergency medical number 911. After any incident, contact your insurer promptly and keep all documentation. Always check your policy wording for exclusions and ask your insurer if you are unsure about cover for certain activities or medical conditions.
claim_checklist: Call 911 for emergency medical help if needed.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Keep all medical reports, receipts, and discharge documents.
Take photos or notes of the incident and any treatment received.
Get written confirmation from the medical provider if evacuation or repatriation is needed.
Submit your claim with all supporting documents within the insurer's time limit.
Check your policy wording for exclusions and ask the insurer if unsure.

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Switzerland
items.body_md:
Medical and hospital costs in Switzerland are high, and providers often expect immediate payment. Non-residents are generally not covered by the Swiss national health insurance system, so travel insurance should include cover for emergency treatment and hospital stays. Medical evacuation cover is also important, as noted by official travel advice.

Adventure sports or higher-risk activities may need disclosure to your insurer in advance to avoid claim issues. Travellers from certain countries may be able to use a GHIC or EHIC for some medically necessary state healthcare, but this does not replace travel insurance for private care, repatriation, or uncovered costs. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer if unsure.

Keep your insurance policy number and the insurer's emergency contact details with you. If you receive treatment, ask for itemised bills and keep all receipts. If you are taking prescription medication, check its legality before travel.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible after any incident.
Keep all medical bills, receipts, and written reports from healthcare providers.
If you paid upfront, request a detailed invoice showing the costs and treatment.
For adventure sports or higher-risk activities, make sure you notified your insurer beforehand as required.
Complete and submit the insurer's claim form with the required documents.
Keep copies of everything you send.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Chile
items.body_md:
Before travelling to Chile, check that your policy covers the cost of local medical treatment and unexpected medical evacuation. This is especially important if you have a health condition or are pregnant. Public and private healthcare can require payment, and ambulance and hospital charges may need to be recovered through your insurer.

Emergency evacuation cover matters in remote areas. For example, Rapa Nui (Easter Island) has only one hospital with limited facilities, so serious conditions may require transfer to mainland Chile. If you plan outdoor or adventure activities, confirm your policy includes those activities and any related rescue or evacuation costs.

Keep your insurance certificate, policy number and the insurer’s emergency contact details with you. In a medical emergency, call 131 for an ambulance, and contact your insurer quickly if you are referred to a medical facility. Always review the policy wording and ask your insurer if you are unsure whether something is covered.
claim_checklist: Call 131 for an ambulance if you need emergency medical help.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible, especially if you are referred to a medical facility.
Keep medical reports, prescriptions, receipts and any hospital discharge documents.
Ask for itemised invoices and proof of payment for all treatment and medicines.
Note the names of facilities and staff involved in your care.
Check your policy wording for notice deadlines and required claim forms.
Submit your claim with your policy number and all supporting documents.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for China
items.body_md:
Healthcare in China is not free and can be very expensive, so you should have cover for medical treatment, hospital stays, and medical evacuation and repatriation. Medical care is widely available in urban areas but limited in remote areas, and international-standard clinics for foreigners can cost much more. Payment is often expected at the time of service, and you may need to ask doctors and dentists to use sterilized equipment.

Traditional domestic health cover such as US Medicare is generally not accepted overseas, and medical evacuation can be very costly if needed for serious illness or injury. Consider high-limit emergency medical coverage and 24/7 emergency assistance to help with language barriers and access to English-speaking care. Check the policy wording for how medical evacuation, pre-authorisation, and hospital admission are handled, and make sure any planned activities are included.

Keep a copy of your insurance certificate and the emergency assistance phone number with you. After an incident, contact the assistance service as soon as possible and keep original bills, receipts, and medical reports for your claim.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer or 24/7 assistance service as soon as possible after the incident
Give your policy number, location, and details of what happened
Ask for itemised bills, receipts, and proof of payment at the time of service
Request medical reports, discharge summaries, or other treatment records
Keep copies of all documents, and obtain a police report if theft or an accident is involved
Submit the claim with the required forms and follow up with your insurer if needed

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Colombia
items.body_md:
Travel insurance is not an entry requirement for Colombia, but medical care in major cities is generally adequate while quality varies widely elsewhere. Private clinics often require advance payment in cash or by credit card, and without proof of travel insurance you may be transferred to a public hospital where care may not meet the standards you expect. Consider a policy that includes medical expense cover and medical evacuation cover, as medical evacuation is strongly recommended for Colombia. A plan with trip cancellation, flight delay, and lost baggage cover may also be useful.

Keep proof of travel insurance and your insurer's emergency contact details with you at all times. If you take prescription medication, confirm it is legal in Colombia and keep it in its original packaging with your doctor’s prescription. Check your policy wording for any planned activities or excursions, and ask your insurer about exclusions. Travelling against official government advice for certain border and northern areas could invalidate your travel insurance.

After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as it is safe to do so and follow their instructions. Keep itemized receipts, medical or police reports, and copies of all documents, and ask your insurer about required documentation and deadlines. Review your policy wording and confirm what is covered before you accept treatment where possible.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as it is safe to do so.
Follow the insurer's instructions for medical care or evacuation.
Keep itemized receipts, invoices, and proof of any payments.
Request written medical or police reports where relevant.
Keep copies and photos of all documents and contact details for providers.
Submit all required forms and documentation before the insurer's deadline.
Ask the insurer to confirm what is not covered if you have time to do so.

items.title: Costa Rica travel insurance: medical cover essentials
items.body_md:
Medical care in Costa Rica is generally of a high standard, but only initial emergency treatment is available without charge for visitors. Subsequent treatment will be charged, and ambulance services in remote areas may vary. Public hospitals offer very good services but can have long waiting times and doctors rarely speak English, while private clinics and hospitals, mainly in San José, provide excellent care but can be expensive and typically require upfront payment.

Your insurance should cover medical treatment costs, repatriation, and medical evacuation, which can be very expensive. Keep accessible funds or a payment method with you, as private doctors and hospitals often ask for payment before providing care. Travel insurance is no longer required for entry to Costa Rica as of April 1, 2022, but it remains a sensible safeguard.

After any medical incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and keep itemized receipts, invoices, and medical reports to support a claim. Check your policy wording for what is included and any exclusions.
claim_checklist: Seek necessary medical care and request itemized invoices and medical reports.
Pay any upfront charges and keep all receipts and proof of payment.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible to confirm the claims process and required documents.
Keep ambulance or medical evacuation invoices and any related receipts.
Complete the claim form and attach all supporting documents.
Submit the claim within your insurer's deadline and keep copies for your records.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Cuba
items.body_md:
Cuba requires visitors to have travel insurance for entry. Your policy must include emergency medical care, hospitalization, emergency medical evacuation and repatriation, and cover the full duration of your stay. Consider at least $50,000 in emergency medical coverage and $100,000 in medical evacuation coverage; higher limits may be appropriate if you plan to visit remote or mountainous areas far from quality medical facilities.

Medical facilities in Cuba are state-run and limited. Hospitals and clinics may lack basic drugs, medical supplies and equipment, and hygiene practices may not meet typical international standards. Emergency medical and evacuation cover is therefore especially important. Keep your insurance documents, policy number, and your insurer's emergency assistance contact details with you at all times, including offline copies.

If you need medical care or have an incident, contact your insurer's assistance line as soon as possible. Be aware that Cuban authorities may prevent you from leaving the country with outstanding medical bills, and medical bills are payable by credit card only. Check your policy wording for exclusions and ask your insurer about coverage for your planned activities and any pre-existing conditions.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as it is safe to do so.
Record the date, time, location and details of the incident.
Keep all receipts, invoices, medical reports and police reports if applicable.
If you receive medical care, ask the facility for itemized bills and medical records.
Pay any required costs by credit card as required in Cuba, and keep proof of payment.
Notify your insurer of any hospital admission or medical evacuation as soon as possible.
Submit your claim with the completed claim form and all supporting documents within the timeframe stated in your policy.
Keep copies of everything you send and follow up with your insurer if needed.

items.title: Travel insurance advice for Czechia
items.body_md:
Medical care in Czechia is generally good and widely available, but care providers may require upfront payment. Your travel insurance should cover medical expenses, hospital stays, and medical evacuation so you are not left paying large bills out of pocket.

If you plan to stay in Czechia for more than 90 days, immigration requirements may ask for a certificate of comprehensive travel and medical insurance covering necessary and urgent care for your whole stay. Keep your insurance certificate, policy number, and insurer contact details with you while travelling.

After an incident, seek necessary medical care and contact your insurer or assistance line as soon as possible. Keep all itemised receipts, invoices, and medical reports, especially if you pay upfront. Review your policy wording and ask your insurer exactly what documents you need to submit a claim.
claim_checklist: Seek necessary medical care and keep all medical reports and receipts.
If you pay upfront, request itemised invoices and proof of payment.
Contact your insurer or assistance line as soon as possible.
Ask your insurer what claim forms and documents are required.
Submit the claim with your policy number, receipts, and medical records.
Keep copies of all documents and correspondence for your records.

items.title: Travel insurance for Germany: what to know
items.body_md:
Germany has excellent healthcare, but private care is expensive and providers often require upfront payment. Travel insurance should include emergency medical treatment, hospital stays, medical evacuation and repatriation. If you are a UK resident, carry a GHIC or EHIC for medically necessary state healthcare, but it is not a substitute for travel insurance. Schengen visa applicants generally need at least €30,000 in medical, evacuation and repatriation cover.

Consider cover for trip cancellation, travel delays and lost baggage alongside emergency medical costs. If you plan outdoor or adventure activities, check that the policy covers them and, where relevant, use an experienced guide from a reputable company.

Keep your insurance policy number, 24-hour emergency assistance contact and any GHIC/EHIC with you while travelling. After an incident, notify your insurer promptly, keep all receipts and reports, and ask for a detailed breakdown of expenses, because German hospitals do not usually provide one automatically. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer if anything is unclear.
claim_checklist: Seek necessary medical care and keep all bills, prescriptions and receipts.
Contact your insurer’s emergency assistance line as soon as reasonably possible.
Request a detailed breakdown of expenses from German hospitals or providers.
Keep any police or incident reports for theft, loss or accidents.
Submit your claim with the insurer’s required forms and supporting documents.
Check your policy wording for deadlines and documentation requirements.

items.title: Dominican Republic travel insurance: what to know
items.body_md:
Public medical facilities in the Dominican Republic can be limited, while private hospitals may offer good standards but can be expensive. Travel health cover should include the cost of treatment abroad and repatriation, because visitors who cannot pay hospital bills have in some cases been stopped from leaving the country until the debt is paid.

If you plan activities such as swimming in fresh water or contact with animals, check that your policy covers any needed medical care and evacuation. Medical evacuation cover back to your home country and repatriation of remains can be particularly relevant, as treatment for some risks, such as rabies after an animal bite, may not be available locally.

Keep your policy documents, insurer contact details and a way to access funds with you. After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and keep receipts and reports. Always check the policy wording and ask the insurer about any exclusions or requirements.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer as soon as possible.
Keep all medical bills, receipts and reports.
Obtain a written medical report or hospital record where possible.
Keep proof of payment and any police or incident reports.
Ask the insurer what documents they require and how to submit them.
Check deadlines and keep copies of everything you send.

items.title: Travel insurance for Egypt: medical costs and evacuation
items.body_md:
For Egypt, make sure your travel insurance covers local medical treatment and unexpected medical evacuation. The emergency ambulance number is 123.

Domestic medical insurance and public health programmes are generally not accepted abroad. Without adequate cover you may face high medical costs, and medical evacuation alone can exceed $50,000. Check your policy for local treatment, emergency care and any planned activities.

Keep your policy wording and your insurer's medical assistance contact details with you. If you need urgent help, call 123 and ask for an ambulance, then contact your insurance or medical assistance company quickly.
claim_checklist: Before travelling, confirm your policy covers local medical treatment and medical evacuation in Egypt.
Carry your policy details and the insurer's emergency medical assistance number.
If you need urgent care, call 123 and ask for an ambulance.
Contact your insurance or medical assistance company as soon as possible.
Keep records of treatment, costs, and any reports to support your claim.
Check the policy wording for any exclusions or requirements linked to planned activities.

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Spain
items.body_md:
Spain provides medically necessary state healthcare to visitors who hold a Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) or European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), but this does not replace travel insurance. You should still have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant.

Before you travel, check that Spain can provide the healthcare you may need and that your policy wording covers the costs you might face. If you need emergency medical help, dial 112 and ask for an ambulance.

Keep your GHIC or EHIC and your insurer and travel provider contact details with you. If you are involved in a serious incident or emergency, contact your travel provider and your insurer. For refunds or changes to travel, speak to your travel provider first, as insurers usually require this before you claim.
claim_checklist: Dial 112 and ask for an ambulance in a medical emergency.
Contact your travel provider and insurer if you are involved in a serious incident or emergency.
Tell them what happened and ask what you need to do next.
If you want a refund or travel change, talk to your travel provider first.
You may be able to make a claim through insurance after speaking to your provider.

items.title: France travel insurance: what to check
items.body_md:
France has high-quality medical facilities, but healthcare is not free for visitors. State healthcare may be available to some travellers with a Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) or valid European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), but treatment is provided on the same basis as for French citizens and is not always free. A GHIC or EHIC is not an alternative to travel insurance, and upfront payment may be required for care.

Travel insurance should include cover for emergency medical expenses, hospital stays, and medical evacuation. Private clinics and hospitals can be especially costly and often require immediate payment, so comprehensive cover can help you avoid large out-of-pocket costs.

Keep your insurance policy details, emergency assistance contact information, and any GHIC or EHIC with you. After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and keep all invoices, receipts, and medical documents. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer about any exclusions, excesses, and claims requirements.
claim_checklist: Seek necessary medical care and keep all invoices, receipts, and medical reports.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as reasonably possible.
If your GHIC or EHIC is used, keep any state healthcare paperwork or proof of treatment.
For theft, loss, or a police matter, file a report with local police and keep a copy.
Complete the insurer's claim form and attach all supporting documents.
Ask your insurer about deadlines, original document requirements, and any excess or exclusions.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for the United Kingdom
items.body_md:
For travel to the United Kingdom, emergency medical cover matters because the NHS does not cover foreign travellers, so you may be liable for hospital bills if you need treatment. Consider a policy with around USD 100,000 in emergency medical coverage and USD 250,000 in medical evacuation coverage, especially if you are over 60, have health issues, or plan to visit rural areas such as the Lake District or Scottish Highlands, where medical transport can be slow and expensive.

If you are a UK resident travelling abroad, a GHIC or EHIC is not a replacement for travel insurance: it does not cover private medical costs, repatriation, or extras such as mountain rescue. Check the policy wording for activity cover, cancellation limits, and any pre-existing medical condition exclusions, and ask the insurer if anything is unclear.

Keep your policy documents, the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance number, and any relevant medical or booking information with you. After an incident, contact the insurer as soon as possible and keep receipts and reports.
claim_checklist: Contact the insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Report any incident or cancellation to the relevant provider.
Keep original receipts, medical reports, and police or transport reports.
Complete the claim form and attach the required documents.
Ask the insurer about deadlines and any missing evidence.

items.title: Travel insurance essentials for Georgia
items.body_md:
From 1 January 2026, all foreign tourists entering Georgia must have valid health and accident insurance for the full period of stay. The policy must provide at least 30,000 GEL in coverage, may be issued by a Georgian or foreign insurer, and should be available in Georgian or English for border and immigration checks.

Medical care is not free for tourists in Georgia; hospital stays and medical evacuation can be very expensive, so look for cover that includes emergency treatment, hospitalisation, and evacuation or repatriation. Outside major cities, medical facilities are limited, which makes emergency assistance and evacuation cover especially important.

Keep a digital and printed copy of your insurance certificate with your passport, and check that the policy wording matches your planned activities and any existing health conditions. After an incident, contact your insurer’s 24/7 assistance line as soon as possible and keep all receipts, medical reports, and police reports.
claim_checklist: Get any necessary medical treatment and keep medical or police reports.
Call your insurer's 24/7 emergency assistance number as soon as it is safe.
Ask for a claim reference number and next steps.
Keep original receipts, invoices, and discharge summaries.
Take photos of any accident scene, injuries, or damaged belongings if relevant.
Submit the claim form and documents before the insurer's deadline.
Follow up in writing if you do not receive confirmation or a decision.

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Greece
items.body_md:
Medical care in Greece is not free for tourists, and you may have to pay for all treatment, including hospital stays and medical evacuation, which can be very expensive. Make sure your travel insurance covers local medical costs and unexpected medical evacuation, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant.

Health care facilities are generally adequate in larger cities, but service quality varies. On smaller islands or in remote areas, you may need a medical evacuation to a central hospital in case of serious illness or injury. Some providers only accept cash and may require upfront payment, so keep your policy details and a way to pay with you.

Before you travel, check that your policy covers medical evacuation and hospital stays, and confirm how to contact your insurer from Greece. Keep the emergency numbers 112 or 166 accessible for an ambulance.
claim_checklist: Call emergency services on 112 or 166 if medical help is needed.
Contact your insurer as soon as reasonably possible.
Keep all receipts, invoices, and itemised bills for medical care.
Ask for a written medical report detailing your diagnosis and treatment.
Submit your claim with the required documents to your insurer.
Follow up with your insurer if you do not receive a response.

items.title: Travel insurance essentials for Hong Kong SAR China
items.body_md:
Medical treatment for uninsured foreign visitors to Hong Kong is expensive, and hospitals may ask for an up-front deposit or a guarantee of payment before admission. Make sure your travel insurance covers hospital stays, doctors' fees, and medical evacuation, because public healthcare is not free and costs can be significant.

In an emergency, call 999 and ask for an ambulance. Contact your insurance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility for treatment. Keep your policy details and the insurer's emergency assistance number with you at all times.

If you plan outdoor or wildlife-related activities, check your policy wording for cover for medical treatment after animal bites or scratches and for any activity exclusions. Always read the policy wording and ask your insurer if you are unsure what is covered.
claim_checklist: Call 999 for emergencies and seek necessary medical care.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Keep all medical reports, receipts, discharge documents, and proof of any deposit or payment you made.
If the incident involves theft, assault, or a traffic accident, report it to the police and obtain a copy of the report.
Complete the insurer's claim form and attach all supporting documents within the time stated in your policy.
Keep copies of everything you submit for your own records.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Croatia
items.body_md:
For Croatia, make sure your travel insurance covers medical expenses and hospital stays, as good health care is available in major cities but may be limited in rural areas and emergency services on islands can be inadequate. Upfront payments for care may be requested, so keep your policy details and means to pay accessible.

Medical evacuation coverage is important, especially if you plan to visit remote areas or the islands; activities such as hiking may require helicopter rescue. Check that your policy includes helicopter rescue and medical evacuation, and consider your physical condition before such activities.

If you are eligible, carry a Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) or European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) to access medically necessary state healthcare in Croatia, but travel insurance is still recommended for costs not covered.

After any incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and follow their claims process. Keep all receipts, medical reports, and any other documentation.
claim_checklist: Seek necessary medical care and keep all receipts and invoices.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Obtain a medical report or discharge summary from the treating facility.
If relevant, file a police report for theft, accident, or other incident.
Submit your claim with all required documentation according to your policy wording.

items.title: Hungary travel insurance essentials
items.body_md:
In Hungary, satisfactory medical care is available but quality varies between public and private facilities, and private clinics can be considerably more expensive. Doctors and hospitals often expect proof of travel insurance or payment before providing services, so a policy with medical expense and hospital stay coverage is important. Medical evacuation coverage is also strongly recommended.

Most care providers may only accept cash payments, and U.S. Medicare does not apply overseas. Check whether your usual health plan covers international care; if not, supplemental cover for medical expenses and evacuation may help. If you are travelling on a Schengen Visa, travel insurance may be required for entry.

If you plan to camp, hike, visit caves, or spend time in rural or forested areas, make sure your policy covers those activities and any emergency transport. If you bring prescription medication, check with Hungarian authorities that it is legal and carry necessary documentation with you.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer or assistance line as soon as possible after an incident.
Keep all receipts, invoices, and proof of payment for medical care or other covered expenses.
Ask medical providers for written reports, discharge summaries, and itemised bills.
For theft, accident, or loss, obtain a police or official report where available.
Save your policy number and emergency contact details with you while travelling.
Submit the claim with the documents your insurer asks for and keep copies.

items.title: Travel insurance guide for Indonesia
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for Indonesia should include comprehensive medical cover. Although the national health insurance scheme (JKN) covers almost the entire population, the quality and availability of care varies greatly by region, with differences in healthcare personnel and facilities. Private hospitals and clinics may require upfront payment or proof of insurance, so check that your policy covers inpatient and outpatient treatment, medication, and doctor fees. [1]

Medical evacuation cover matters especially if you travel outside major cities or to remote islands, as local facilities may not be able to handle serious injury or illness. Confirm that your policy includes medically necessary evacuation by air or road to a suitable hospital in Indonesia or a neighbouring country. [1]

The official tourism site highlights renting cars, motorcycles, or using local transport, and visiting sites like Borobudur with many stone steps. Check whether your policy covers these activities, including accidental injury and personal liability for damage or injury to others. Keep your policy number, the 24-hour emergency assistance contact, and copies of your passport, receipts, and medical documents with you at all times. [2]

After an incident, contact your insurer’s emergency line as soon as you can, and ask before agreeing to large treatment or evacuation costs if possible. Keep all original bills, police reports (for theft or accidents), and hospital discharge summaries, and check your policy wording for any country-specific exclusions or requirements. [1][2]
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's 24/7 emergency assistance number immediately.
Keep all original receipts, invoices, and medical reports.
For accidents or theft, obtain a police report as soon as possible.
Document any evacuation or transport arrangements with written approval from the insurer.
Submit the claim form and supporting documents within the timeframe stated in your policy.
Keep a copy of all correspondence and documents for your records.

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Ireland
items.body_md:
In Ireland, public health facilities may be available to residents, but visitors should not assume care is free; many services require co-payments for patients who are not fully eligible citizens, so travel insurance for medical costs is important. Private medical care may also involve significant charges, and emergency evacuation coverage can help if you need transport to appropriate treatment.

Check policy wording for medical expenses, hospitalisation, emergency evacuation, cancellation and theft cover before you travel. Keep your policy number, emergency assistance contact and proof of insurance with you during the trip.

Before receiving non-emergency care in Ireland, check with the healthcare facility and your insurance provider about costs and cover. After an incident, contact your insurer promptly and keep all receipts, reports and medical documentation to support a claim.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer or emergency assistance line as soon as possible after the incident.
Keep receipts, invoices and itemised bills for medical treatment or other covered costs.
Obtain a medical report or discharge summary if you received treatment.
For theft or loss, get a written report from local authorities or the relevant provider.
Check your policy wording for required claim forms and deadlines.
Submit the completed claim form with supporting documents.
Follow up with the insurer if you do not receive confirmation.

items.title: Travel insurance for India
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for India should include cover for hospital treatment and emergency medical evacuation. Healthcare quality varies significantly: care in major cities can be good, but it may be limited or unavailable in rural areas, and private facilities can be expensive. Many hospitals require up-front payment or confirmation of insurance coverage before starting treatment.

If you need urgent help, dial 112 and ask for an ambulance. Contact your insurance or medical assistance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility. Keep your policy number, the insurer’s emergency contact details, and any payment guarantee information with you. Check your policy wording carefully for what is covered, including evacuation and any activities you plan to do, and ask the insurer if anything is unclear.

After an incident or treatment, report to your insurer as soon as possible. Keep itemised bills, receipts, medical reports, and any other documents the provider gives you, as private care often involves out-of-pocket costs. Ask your insurer about the next steps rather than assuming a cost will be covered.
claim_checklist: Get medical help if needed and call 112 for an ambulance in an emergency.
Contact your insurer or medical assistance company as soon as possible, especially if you are referred for treatment.
If a hospital asks for up-front payment, keep all receipts and ask for itemised bills.
Collect medical reports, discharge summaries, and a letter stating the diagnosis and treatment.
Keep proof of any other expenses such as transport, accommodation changes, or medication.
Submit the claim with the required forms and documents according to your policy wording.
Follow up with the insurer if you do not receive confirmation or have questions.

items.title: Travel insurance for Iceland
items.body_md:
Health care in Iceland is excellent, but services can be limited outside urban areas. Visitors are generally not covered by Iceland’s national health insurance system, so nonresidents may need to pay medical costs upfront. Emergency medical treatment and medically necessary transportation between facilities, especially from rural or remote areas, can be costly. Travel insurance that includes coverage for medical expenses, hospital stays, and medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

If you plan outdoor activities such as hiking, glacier travel, or visits to remote areas, consider coverage that includes helicopter rescue and medical evacuation. Confirm that your policy covers your planned activities and that your physical condition is suitable for them. Travel with companions and never go alone in challenging environments.

Keep your insurance policy details, emergency assistance contact numbers, and proof of coverage with you during the trip. After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible, keep all receipts, reports, and medical records, and ask your insurer about approved facilities and payment procedures. Check the policy wording for exclusions, coverage limits, and required documentation before you travel.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer’s emergency assistance line as soon as it is safe to do so.
Keep all medical reports, receipts, invoices, and payment records.
Record the names of medical facilities, treating staff, and dates of treatment.
Obtain a written medical certificate or report describing the incident or condition.
Ask your insurer which claim forms and documents are required before submitting.
Submit the claim with copies of all documents, keeping the originals for your records.

items.title: Travel insurance for Italy: what to look for
items.body_md:
Travel insurance is not required for entry to Italy, but U.S. health insurance, including Medicare, is generally not accepted. Without suitable cover, you could pay substantial out-of-pocket costs for emergency medical treatment, so look for a policy with solid limits for medical expenses, hospital stays and emergency medical evacuation, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant.

Healthcare in Italy is generally high-quality and affordable for tourists, and private clinics and hospitals that cater to foreign travellers are available. Hospital services may be limited in rural areas. If your trip includes hiking in the Dolomites or other active excursions, check that your policy covers those activities and includes emergency medical evacuation.

If you need urgent medical help, dial 118 and ask for an ambulance. Contact your insurance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility for treatment. Keep your policy information and emergency assistance contact with you, and check the policy wording or ask your insurer about activity-specific or medical coverage questions before you travel.
claim_checklist: If urgent, call 118 and get medical treatment first.
Contact your insurer's assistance line as soon as possible, especially if you are referred to a medical facility.
Keep all medical reports, receipts, prescriptions and discharge documents.
Record the date, provider and reason for treatment.
Submit your claim with the required documents within the deadline stated in your policy.
Check your policy wording before travelling to confirm what medical and activity costs are covered.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Jordan
items.body_md:
In Jordan, you generally need to pay for all medical care, and cash payment is often required immediately for procedures. Health services in Amman can be modern and private, but outside major cities facilities may be basic or inadequate, so cover for hospital stays and treatment costs is important.

Medical evacuation can be very expensive and may be needed for serious illness or injury, especially outside Amman; ambulance and paramedic services are limited compared with some other countries. Check that your policy includes emergency medical evacuation and repatriation cover, and review the wording for any exclusions or pre-authorisation requirements.

Keep your policy number, insurer’s emergency assistance phone number, proof of cover, ID, and relevant medical information with you. If you are injured or become ill, call 911 for an ambulance if needed. Contact your insurer quickly if you are referred to a medical facility for treatment, and ask what documents or approvals are needed before paying large cash amounts where possible.
claim_checklist: Call 911 for emergency medical help if needed.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible, especially if you are referred for treatment or admitted to hospital.
Ask the medical provider for itemised receipts and invoices for any cash payments.
Keep copies of medical reports, discharge summaries, and prescriptions.
Ask your insurer about any pre-authorisation or approved facilities before evacuation or major treatment.
Check your policy wording for claim deadlines and required documents.
Submit your claim with all supporting documents as instructed by the insurer.

items.title: Japan Travel Insurance: Key Cover and Claim Steps
items.body_md:
Japan does not require travel insurance for entry, but U.S. health insurance is generally not accepted and foreign visitors may need to pay in full at the time of treatment or show proof of ability to pay. Strong travel medical coverage is recommended even for young, healthy travelers.

A comprehensive policy should include medical treatment, hospital stays, and medical evacuation. Cancellation cover is also useful because Japan has high travel costs and risks from natural disasters that can cause significant financial loss.

Keep your policy number, insurer’s emergency contact details, and proof of coverage or ability to pay with you. In an emergency, dial 119 for an ambulance. Contact your insurer quickly if you are referred to a medical facility, and check your policy wording and ask your insurer about any exclusions, including pre-existing conditions.
claim_checklist: Call 119 for an ambulance if there is a medical emergency.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible, especially if referred for treatment.
Keep all medical reports, itemized bills, receipts, and proof of payment.
Ask the medical facility for documentation showing the diagnosis and treatment.
Note any insurer notice periods and required claim documents from your policy wording.
Submit the claim with the requested documents and follow up with the insurer.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Kenya
items.body_md:
For Kenya, check that your policy covers local medical treatment and emergency medical evacuation, particularly if you have a health condition or are pregnant. Medical resources can be limited, and evacuation from remote national parks or coastal areas can be costly, so consider a plan with at least $100,000 in emergency medical coverage and at least $250,000 in medical evacuation coverage.

Kenya requires visitors to have at least $50,000 in cumulative medical protection, and is rolling out travel health insurance requirements for non-Kenyan visitors staying less than 12 months. Keep your policy details and your insurer's emergency contact number with you while travelling.

If you need urgent help, dial 999 and ask for an ambulance. Contact your insurance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility, and keep all receipts, reports and proof of expenses for any claim.
claim_checklist: Seek medical help first: dial 999 for an ambulance in an emergency.
Notify your insurer as soon as possible or when referred to a medical facility.
Keep medical reports, receipts, prescriptions, and any police or incident reports.
Record names of facilities, dates, and contact details of treating staff.
Follow the insurer's instructions before arranging evacuation or non-emergency treatment, if possible.
Submit the completed claim form with all supporting documents within the insurer's deadline.

items.title: Travel insurance for Cambodia: medical cover, evacuation and claims
items.body_md:
Medical facilities in Cambodia are poor and limited outside some foreign hospitals in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, and doctors or hospitals may require cash payment or a written guarantee from insurers before providing care. Medical evacuation to Thailand or Singapore is often needed to get adequate treatment, so look for a policy with strong inpatient and emergency medical cover plus medical evacuation and repatriation benefits.

Basic travel health insurance for Cambodia can cost around $100–$120 per month for essential inpatient and emergency coverage, while comprehensive expat plans may run $240–$360 per month with outpatient, dental and maternity benefits. Local plans can start from about $80 per month but often offer only regional medical coverage, so check benefit limits and whether the insurer can pay providers directly or you will need to pay upfront and claim back.

Common risks noted for Cambodia include motor vehicle crashes, animal bites that may require rabies treatment, and mosquito-borne diseases. If you plan motorized travel or outdoor activities, review policy exclusions and activity cover with your insurer. After an incident, contact your insurer's assistance line as soon as possible, seek care in Phnom Penh or Siem Reap where better options exist, and keep all receipts and reports. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer about anything you are unsure of.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's 24/7 emergency assistance number as soon as it is safe.
Notify the hospital or clinic that you have insurance and ask whether the insurer can provide a payment guarantee.
Collect itemized medical bills, discharge summaries and receipts for any cash payments.
Keep police or incident reports for road accidents, theft or animal bites.
Save all transport and evacuation paperwork if you are moved to Thailand, Singapore or elsewhere.
Submit the completed claim form and supporting documents within the deadline stated in your policy wording.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for South Korea
items.body_md:
South Korea has good medical and dental care, but it can be expensive, and there is no free healthcare for tourists. Your travel insurance should cover hospital stays, doctor visits, prescribed medicines, medical evacuation, and repatriation of remains. Check whether the policy includes medical evacuation to your home country if needed, and ask the insurer about any pre-existing condition wording. Medical tourism is common, so if you plan any procedure, choose providers carefully and confirm how your policy handles complications.

Payment is usually expected at the time of service, and Korean medical institutions generally will not bill your insurer directly. Keep your insurer’s contact details and policy number with you, along with emergency number 119 for an ambulance. Private hospitals in cities are often better staffed and equipped than public or rural facilities.

If you need treatment, call 119 for an ambulance in an emergency and contact your insurance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility. Keep receipts and medical reports, and check the policy wording for the claims process rather than assuming the provider will handle payment.
claim_checklist: Call 119 for an ambulance in an emergency.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible if you are referred for treatment.
Ask the medical facility for itemised bills and medical reports.
Keep receipts for hospital stays, doctor visits, and prescribed medicines.
Do not expect the hospital to bill your insurer directly; you may need to pay upfront.
Check your policy wording for required documents and deadlines.
Submit your claim to the insurer using the documents they request.

items.title: Travel insurance basics for Laos
items.body_md:
Medical care in Laos is very limited: facilities are basic, and outside the capital there may be no reliable services for emergencies. Make sure your travel insurance includes cover for all medical costs overseas, because medical care is not free and hospitals may require up-front payment. Evacuation assistance is essential, as moving to a better-equipped hospital in another country can be difficult and expensive.

Check your policy wording carefully for what is and is not covered. Consider whether you need trip cancellation cover, and if you plan adventure activities such as caving, confirm that injuries, evacuation and medical treatment related to those activities are included. Look at the Product Disclosure Statement or equivalent and ask your insurer directly about any exclusions or limits.

Carry your insurance details with you, including emergency contact numbers for the assistance provider. If you are bitten or scratched by an animal, seek care promptly and contact your insurer; rabies risks may be relevant for some travellers, but vaccination decisions should be discussed with a health professional. Keep receipts and documentation for any paid medical care.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as it is safe.
Keep all medical reports, receipts and proof of payment.
Note dates, locations and contact details of any hospitals or clinics.
If evacuated or transported, keep paperwork from the transport provider.
Report any animal bites or incidents to local authorities if needed.
Submit the claim with required forms and copies of documents.
Follow up in writing if you do not receive a response.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Morocco
items.body_md:
In Morocco, tourists must pay for all medical care, and public health facilities provide limited medical care. Private clinics in major cities generally offer a higher standard, but treatment and hospital stays can still be very expensive. Make sure your travel insurance includes cover for medical treatment costs, hospital stays, medical evacuation, and repatriation, and check the policy wording to confirm what is and is not covered.

Medical care standards vary greatly across the country. Casablanca, Marrakesh and Rabat have good private facilities for non-emergencies, but services can be extremely limited in smaller cities and rural or remote areas. Doctors and hospitals often expect immediate cash payment, and credit card payment is not always available, so keep accessible funds and your insurance documents with you.

Before you travel, read the Product Disclosure Statement or policy wording carefully and ask your insurer about cover for any planned activities. If you need medical attention, contact your insurer as soon as possible, keep all receipts and medical reports, and confirm the claims process and any cash payment reimbursement requirements with the insurer.
claim_checklist: Seek urgent medical care if needed and ask the provider for detailed invoices and medical reports.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Keep all receipts, discharge papers, prescriptions, and proof of payment, including cash payment records.
Obtain a written medical report or doctor's note describing the treatment and diagnosis.
Note whether payments were made in cash or by card and keep any currency exchange records.
Submit the claim using the insurer's required forms and evidence, and check deadlines in your policy wording.

items.title: Mexico travel insurance: medical costs, evacuation and claims
items.body_md:
Medical costs and emergency evacuation are the main cover to check for Mexico. Healthcare quality varies by area, and not all hospitals will bill insurers directly; many providers expect cash or upfront payment, and U.S. health insurance is not widely accepted. Make sure your policy includes doctor visits, hospital stays, diagnostic tests, medicines, and emergency medical evacuation, including from high-altitude places such as Mexico City. If you plan adventure activities, check the policy wording for exclusions or ask your insurer whether those activities are covered.

Keep your insurance documents, the insurer’s 24-hour emergency contact number, ID, and payment method with you, preferably in both paper and digital form. If you need urgent help, dial 911 and ask for an ambulance. Ask the insurer before non-emergency treatment whether they can arrange direct billing; if you must pay first, get itemised receipts and medical reports. For disputes over medical services, PROFECO may be able to assist, but this is not legal advice.

After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and follow their claims process. Collect all itemised bills, discharge paperwork, prescriptions, and proof of payment. If emergency evacuation is needed, use the insurer’s assistance line rather than arranging transport yourself unless immediate danger. Always check your policy wording for exclusions, pre-existing condition rules, and activity-specific limits, and ask the insurer if anything is unclear.
claim_checklist: Call 911 for an ambulance if you need immediate medical help.
Contact your insurer’s 24-hour emergency assistance line as soon as you can.
If care providers require payment upfront, pay and request itemised receipts.
Keep all medical reports, discharge papers, prescriptions, and proof of payment.
Submit your claim using the insurer’s forms and include all documents.
If you have a dispute over medical services, ask your insurer and consider whether PROFECO can help.

items.title: Malaysia travel insurance guidance
items.body_md:
In Malaysia, government and private hospitals charge for all services, and private healthcare is expensive. Good quality care is mainly available in major cities, with significant variation elsewhere. Ensure your travel insurance covers local treatment costs and hospital stays.

Travel insurance should include medical evacuation cover, as this is consistently recommended by official sources. The emergency medical number is 999; ask for an ambulance if needed. Payment is expected at the time of service, either in cash or by major credit card.

If you plan outdoor or rural travel, consider risks such as rabies where treatment may not be readily available, and discuss vaccination with a health professional before you go. Check your policy wording for exclusions and ask your insurer about activities you intend to do.
claim_checklist: Call 999 and ask for an ambulance if you need emergency medical help.
Contact your travel insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as you can after an incident.
Ask the hospital for receipts and medical reports, as you may have to pay upfront and claim later.
Keep proof of any cash or card payments for treatment, medicines, or evacuation.
Notify your insurer before arranging any non-emergency medical evacuation if possible.

items.title: Travel insurance for the Netherlands
items.body_md:
In the Netherlands, visitors who are eligible can use a UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) or European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) to access medically necessary state healthcare. This can reduce treatment costs in the public system, but it does not cover private care or repatriation, so travel insurance is still worth considering. Check your policy for medical expenses and emergency medical evacuation if you might need to return home for treatment.

If you are travelling from outside the EU or UK, your regular health insurance may provide limited or no cover in the Netherlands. For example, Medicare generally does not pay for care outside the United States, and other plans may have similar restrictions. Unexpected hospital or ambulance costs can still arise, so consider cover for medical treatment, hospital stays, and any planned activities. Read the policy wording for exclusions and confirm with the insurer if an activity is covered.

Keep your GHIC or EHIC, your travel insurance certificate, and your insurer’s 24-hour emergency contact number with you. After an incident, seek necessary care, notify your insurer as soon as possible, and save all receipts, invoices, discharge letters, and proof of payment. If you use a GHIC or EHIC, show it at the point of care and keep any co-payment records.
claim_checklist: Get the treatment you need and ask for itemised invoices and a medical report.
Contact your insurer’s emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
If you have a GHIC or EHIC, show it when receiving state healthcare and keep any co-payment receipts.
Collect all documents: receipts, prescriptions, discharge papers, and proof of payment.
Complete the claim form from your insurer and attach the requested documents.
Submit the claim within the time limit stated in your policy.
Keep copies of everything and follow up with the insurer if you do not hear back.

items.title: Norway Travel Insurance Coverage Essentials
items.body_md:
Medical care in Norway is generally high quality and widely available, but access to emergency assistance can be very limited in Arctic and remote regions. Consider coverage for medical expenses, hospital stays and, especially, medical evacuation or helicopter rescue. Emergency services are reached by calling 113, and medical staff commonly speak English.

Non-emergency care can be expensive for tourists without a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC), so check what your policy covers before treatment. Policies often exclude intentional acts, illegal activities, travel against official government advice, and alcohol- or drug-related incidents.

Before adventure or outdoor activities, get detailed information and ensure your policy includes helicopter rescue and medical evacuation. Carry prescription medication in its original packaging with your doctor’s prescription, and check with Norwegian authorities that the medication is legal in Norway.

After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and keep receipts, medical reports and any police or incident documentation. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer about specific coverage and exclusions rather than relying on general guidance.
claim_checklist: Call 113 for medical emergencies if you need urgent help.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible and follow their claims instructions.
Save all receipts, invoices, medical records and police or incident reports.
Keep prescription medication in original packaging with your doctor’s prescription during travel.
Before activities, confirm your policy covers helicopter rescue and medical evacuation.
Check policy wording for exclusions and ask your insurer if anything is unclear.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for New Zealand
items.body_md:
Medical care in New Zealand is generally good, but visitors can face serious costs for illness or serious injury. New Zealand’s public accident scheme (ACC) may cover some costs if you are injured in an accident, but it usually does not cover illnesses, ongoing care after you leave, or medical evacuation. Check that your travel insurance includes hospital stays, medical treatment, and medical evacuation, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant.

Some short-term visitors may have limited access to public care through reciprocal health agreements, but these do not cover everything. Keep your insurance policy number, insurer’s emergency contact details, and any relevant medical information with you. If you need urgent help, call 111 and ask for an ambulance. Contact your insurer quickly if you are referred to a medical facility for treatment.
claim_checklist: Call 111 for an ambulance if it is an emergency.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible after the incident or referral.
Keep all receipts, invoices, medical reports, and any police or accident reports.
Ask the medical facility for itemised bills and discharge paperwork.
Submit your claim using the insurer’s required forms and documents.
Check your policy wording for time limits and required proof.

items.title: Oman travel insurance: key cover and claims steps
items.body_md:
Medical care in Oman may require using private health facilities, and visitors who cannot settle medical charges may be stopped from leaving the country. Your policy should include adequate cover for medical treatment, hospital stays, and repatriation, and you should have accessible funds to pay any upfront costs because immediate cash payment is often required.

Check that your policy covers medical evacuation, including helicopter rescue if you plan remote or adventure activities, and always use a reputable guide for such trips. Consider cover for insect-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, and leishmaniasis, and take precautions like using insect repellent and anti-malarial medication if advised. Heat-related illness is also a risk in summer.

Keep your policy number, emergency assistance contact, and proof of insurance with you, along with a way to access funds for medical bills. After an incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible, keep all receipts and reports, and ask the insurer what documents they need before paying or signing anything. Check the policy wording for exclusions and limits.
claim_checklist: Contact your travel insurer’s emergency assistance line as soon as possible after becoming ill or injured.
Keep all medical bills, receipts, prescriptions, and discharge documents.
If you need evacuation or hospital admission, get approval from the insurer if the policy requires it.
Ask the medical provider for an itemised invoice in English where possible.
Keep a record of any police or incident report if the claim involves theft, accident, or adventure activity.
Submit your claim with the completed form and supporting documents within the time limit stated in your policy.
Check the policy wording or ask the insurer if you are unsure what is covered.

items.title: Travel Insurance Guidance for Peru
items.body_md:
When visiting Peru, prioritise cover for medical treatment costs and emergency medical evacuation, as medical care may be limited outside Lima and is not free for foreign visitors. If you plan high-altitude trekking or adventure sports, confirm your policy includes those activities.

Keep your insurance policy details, insurer's emergency contact number, and the local emergency number 106 with you at all times. Medical facilities can be harder to access outside Lima, so having quick access to these details can help.

After an incident, contact your insurer promptly and keep all receipts, medical reports, and proof of travel. Review your policy wording for the correct claims procedure and ask the insurer if you are unsure about cover or required documents.
claim_checklist: Call emergency number 106 if urgent medical help is needed.
Obtain and keep all medical reports, bills, and receipts.
Contact your travel insurer as soon as possible after the incident.
Follow the insurer's instructions for starting a claim.
Provide any documents the insurer requests, such as proof of travel and treatment.
Check your policy wording for time limits and required documentation.

items.title: Philippines travel insurance: cover and claims
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for the Philippines should include cover for private medical treatment and unexpected medical evacuation. Public medical facilities can lack basic resources and supplies, especially in rural areas, and hospitals and doctors often ask for payment upfront before treatment or admission. Ambulance services may be limited or unable to provide medical care during transport, and patients may have to bear all costs for transfer between hospitals.

If you are travelling for cosmetic or elective surgery, research the provider carefully and check whether your policy covers complications, follow-up care, and medical evacuation. Keep your policy documents and emergency contact details with you, and expect that you may need to pay costs upfront and claim later. Always check the policy wording and ask your insurer if you are unsure what is covered.
claim_checklist: Call 911 and ask for an ambulance if you need emergency medical help.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance team as soon as possible.
Ask the hospital or clinic for itemised bills, receipts, and medical reports at the time of treatment.
Keep proof of any upfront payments and any costs for transfer between hospitals.
If you require medical evacuation, check with your insurer whether you need approval first.
Submit your claim with all supporting documents as soon as you can.

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Poland
items.body_md:
In Poland, medical providers often require payment up front, usually by cash or card, so your travel insurance should cover medical costs and make it clear how you can claim reimbursement. U.S. Medicare is not valid overseas, and UK residents may use a GHIC or EHIC for medically necessary state healthcare, but this is not a substitute for travel insurance.

Medical evacuation cover is strongly recommended, as hospital facilities and nursing support may not match home standards in all regions. Emergency services can be limited in small towns and rural areas, and English-speaking staff may be scarce, especially outside major cities. In an emergency, call 112.

Keep all receipts, medical reports, and proof of payment. Before you travel, check your policy wording for exclusions, coverage for pre-existing conditions, and any requirement to contact the insurer before non-emergency treatment. Carry your insurance details and, if eligible, your GHIC or EHIC.
claim_checklist: Call 112 for an ambulance in a medical emergency.
Pay the provider up front and ask for an itemized receipt.
Keep all medical reports, prescriptions, and proof of payment.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible and follow their claims process.
If you used an EHIC or GHIC, keep any state healthcare paperwork alongside your insurance claim.
Submit the claim with the receipts and any supporting documents requested by your insurer.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Portugal
items.body_md:
Portugal does not legally require travel insurance for short tourist stays, but it is strongly recommended because tourists are not covered by the public healthcare system and treatment can be costly. Medical facilities are generally good, though public clinics and hospitals may be overwhelmed and rural facilities can be limited. Many private hospitals and clinics ask for advance payment or proof of insurance before treatment.

Check that your policy includes emergency medical treatment and hospital stays, medical evacuation, and repatriation. If you need a Schengen visa, you will typically need at least €30,000 in emergency medical, evacuation, and repatriation coverage. UK residents with a valid GHIC or EHIC can access medically necessary state healthcare, but this does not replace travel insurance.

Keep your insurance details, passport, and any GHIC/EHIC with you. After an incident, contact your insurer’s 24/7 assistance line as soon as possible, keep all receipts and reports, and confirm what is covered before agreeing to private treatment. Always check your policy wording and ask your insurer if you are unsure.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer’s 24/7 assistance line as soon as possible after the incident.
Keep all receipts, medical reports, police reports, and proof of payment.
Ask the hospital or clinic for an itemised invoice and any medical documentation.
If you used a GHIC or EHIC, keep a record of where and when it was used.
Submit your claim with the required forms and supporting documents within the insurer’s deadline.
Check your policy wording for exclusions, limits, and required notification times.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Qatar
items.body_md:
Medical care in Qatar is expensive and tourists must pay for all treatment, including hospital stays and emergency evacuation, because there is no reciprocal free healthcare agreement. Make sure your travel insurance covers medical costs, hospitalisation, evacuation, and repatriation to your home country.

If you stay longer than 30 days, Qatari law requires you to buy health insurance from a company approved by the Ministry of Public Health, either before or on arrival. This mandatory policy only covers medical treatment in Qatar and does not cover other travel problems like lost luggage, so you still need a separate comprehensive travel policy for those risks.

Check your policy wording for trip cancellation coverage and ask your insurer about evacuation assistance and any planned activities. Keep your policy details and emergency assistance contact information with you at all times.
claim_checklist: Notify your insurer as soon as possible after an incident.
Keep all receipts, medical reports, and police reports if applicable.
Obtain written documentation from any medical provider you visit.
Keep your policy number and emergency assistance contact details handy.
Submit your claim using the required forms and provide all evidence.
Check your policy wording for time limits and exclusions before submitting.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Saudi Arabia
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for Saudi Arabia should cover emergency medical treatment and medical evacuation. Healthcare facilities in major Saudi cities are of a high standard, but most towns have only a health centre or basic hospital, so you may need to be moved for serious care. Saudi Arabia requires visitors to have health insurance as part of the visa process, but that basic eVisa cover may be limited; check your own policy wording to see what it adds for local treatment or evacuation.

Also consider cover for trip cancellation and any planned activities. Keep your policy details and the insurer's emergency contact number with you at all times, along with any documents the insurer asks you to carry. If you have a health condition or are pregnant, check before you travel that the healthcare you may need is available and that your policy covers it.

After an incident, seek any immediate medical help you need and contact your insurer as soon as possible. Keep all bills, receipts, medical reports and official documents. Follow the claims process in your policy wording, and ask the insurer if anything is unclear.
