claim_checklist: Get any urgent medical help you need and keep all bills, receipts and medical reports.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as you can.
Give your policy number and explain what happened, where and when.
Keep any police, incident or medical reports that support your claim.
Send the documents your insurer asks for within the time limit in your policy.
Check your policy wording for exclusions or excess amounts, and ask the insurer if unsure.

items.title: Travel insurance basics for Sweden
items.body_md:
Health care in Sweden is generally excellent, and English is widely spoken in main hospitals, especially in Stockholm, Malmö, and Gothenburg. However, visitors who are not residents are normally expected to pay their own medical costs in full, and many providers may only accept payment at the time of care. Check whether your existing health plan covers overseas treatment and whether it pays providers directly or reimburses you later.

Travel insurance should include cover for hospital stays and medical evacuation. Emergency services may be limited in remote areas, so if your trip involves outdoor activities or travel outside urban centres, consider cover that includes helicopter rescue or medical evacuation. For UK residents, a GHIC or EHIC may help with medically necessary state healthcare, but it is not a replacement for travel insurance.

In Sweden, travel cover for 45 days is often included in home insurance, and some bank card purchases may also include cover. Check the policy wording and ask your insurer about limits, activities, and how to access help. Keep your insurer's emergency contact details and policy number with you while travelling.

If you need urgent help, dial 112 and ask for an ambulance. After any incident, contact your insurer as soon as reasonably possible and keep all receipts, medical reports, and official documents to support a claim.
claim_checklist: Get medical help or safety assistance first; call 112 for an ambulance or emergency services if needed.
Contact your insurer or their assistance line as soon as reasonably possible.
Keep all receipts, invoices, discharge papers, and any police or incident reports.
Ask for a written medical report or certificate if you receive treatment.
Complete the insurer's claim form and attach proof of payment and supporting documents.
Check with the insurer about deadlines and any missing information, then follow up as needed.

items.title: Travel insurance considerations for Singapore
items.body_md:
Medical care in Singapore is high quality but expensive. Hospitals and doctors generally expect immediate payment by credit card or cash, may not accept foreign health insurance, and can require a substantial deposit before major treatment. Make sure your policy covers inpatient and outpatient treatment, medical evacuation, and repatriation, because these costs can be very high.

There is no reciprocal healthcare agreement for many visitors. For example, the Australian Government won't pay medical costs, and U.S. Medicare does not apply overseas. Carry enough prescribed medication for your stay in your hand baggage, and keep your policy details and emergency assistance number with you.

English is widely spoken in hospitals, which helps in an emergency. Before buying, check the policy wording for any exclusions, activity coverage, and how upfront payment is handled; ask the insurer if you are unsure.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as it is safe.
Tell the hospital or clinic you have travel insurance and ask what documents they can provide.
Keep all receipts, invoices, and proof of upfront payments.
Request a detailed medical report and discharge summary.
If police are involved, obtain a copy of the police report.
Submit your claim with the insurer's required forms and documents within the time limit.
Keep copies of everything for your records.

items.title: Travel insurance in Thailand: what to look for
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for Thailand should include cover for private and public hospital treatment, because healthcare is not free for tourists and payment is often expected at the point of care. Private hospitals in Bangkok may ask for a large deposit before non-emergency treatment, and many providers accept cash rather than credit cards. Look for a policy with direct billing, as some insurers can arrange payment with Thai hospitals, which can make treatment smoother.

Also check that your policy covers unexpected medical evacuation, especially if you have a health condition or are pregnant. Mosquito-borne and food- or waterborne illnesses are common concerns, and flooding is the most frequent natural disaster, so cover for weather-related disruption and urgent medical care is worth considering. If you plan adventure activities, confirm with your insurer that they are included.

Keep your policy details, emergency assistance number and proof of coverage with you while travelling. In an emergency in Thailand, you can call 191 or 1669 for an ambulance. After any incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and ask what documents they require.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer or their emergency assistance line as soon as it is safe to do so.
Keep all receipts, invoices and medical reports from Thai hospitals or clinics.
Ask the hospital for a detailed bill and diagnosis or treatment summary in English if possible.
If police or local authorities are involved, obtain a copy of the report.
Ask your insurer about direct billing or whether you must pay first and claim later.
Submit documents according to your policy wording and keep copies for your records.

items.title: Tunisia travel insurance: key cover to consider
items.body_md:
Make sure your policy includes cover for medical treatment in Tunisia and repatriation, and that you have accessible funds for costs you may need to pay upfront if care is billed locally. Medical evacuation cover is worth considering, especially because serious conditions such as rabies may require rapid treatment that is not always available in every area. Check whether your insurer provides evacuation assistance and medical cover, and how to contact them from Tunisia.

If you are bitten, scratched, or have close contact with animals, seek medical attention promptly and keep documentation. Prescription medications available in Tunisia may differ from what you are used to or be hard to find, so carry enough of your own supplies and keep them in original packaging where possible. Avoid animal contact and supervise children closely.

Traffic crashes are a leading cause of serious injury for travellers, so reasonable medical and evacuation limits matter. Before buying, check the policy wording for exclusions, pre-existing conditions, and what you must do in an emergency; ask the insurer if anything is unclear.
claim_checklist: Get medical care or police help as soon as it is safe to do so.
Contact your insurer or emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Keep all receipts, invoices, medical reports, and police reports.
If bitten or scratched by an animal, keep details of treatment dates and providers.
Take photos of documents and any relevant incident scene if possible.
Submit the claim form with copies of all supporting documents.
Follow up in writing and keep your own copy of everything.

items.title: Travel insurance for Türkiye: what to look for
items.body_md:
Medical care in Türkiye varies greatly by location and facility. Private hospitals in major cities such as Ankara, Antalya, Izmir, and Istanbul may have modern equipment and international accreditation, but healthcare standards can be lower in smaller cities, and some facilities may not be able to treat certain serious conditions. Make sure your policy includes adequate medical coverage for local treatment and unexpected medical evacuation.

Hospitals in Türkiye often require foreign travellers to pay upfront for care. Check whether your policy provides direct payment to hospitals or guarantees payment, as this can help you avoid high out-of-pocket costs. This is particularly important if you have a health condition, are pregnant, or plan any medical treatment abroad; verify that planned procedures and providers authorized by the Turkish Ministry of Health are covered under the policy wording.

In an emergency, dial 112 and ask for an ambulance. Keep your policy number and insurer’s emergency contact details with you, and contact your insurance or medical assistance company promptly if you are referred to a medical facility. After an incident, keep all receipts, medical reports, and proof of payment to support a claim.
claim_checklist: Dial 112 and ask for an ambulance in a medical emergency.
Contact your insurer or medical assistance company as soon as you are referred to a medical facility.
Keep copies of medical reports, prescriptions, and hospital paperwork.
Ask the facility for an itemized invoice and proof of payment.
Check the policy wording for medical evacuation, upfront payment, and planned treatment coverage before you travel.
Notify your insurer about any follow-up care or changes in your condition.
Submit all required documentation within the time frame stated in your policy.

items.title: Travel insurance for Taiwan: what to know
items.body_md:
Medical care in Taiwan is generally good, especially in major cities, but tourists usually must pay for all treatment. Hospitals and clinics often require up-front payment, and many accept only cash. For serious illness or injury, medical evacuation may be necessary and can be very expensive, so your policy should include coverage for medical treatment, hospital stays, and medical evacuation.

There is no reciprocal healthcare or free treatment for most foreign visitors, and your home government will not pay your medical bills. Before travelling, check that your health insurance or travel insurance provides overseas coverage and includes medical evacuation. Emergency ambulances can be called on 119.

After any incident, keep all receipts, medical reports, and proof of payment, and contact your insurer as soon as possible. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer about their required process for treatment approval, evacuation, and claims.
claim_checklist: Seek medical help immediately; call 119 for an ambulance if needed.
Keep all receipts, itemised invoices, medical reports, and proof of any up-front cash payments.
Contact your insurer or their emergency assistance line as soon as possible.
Follow the insurer's instructions before arranging non-emergency treatment or medical evacuation.
Obtain medical certificates and reports, preferably in English, showing diagnosis, treatment, and dates.
Submit your claim with the insurer's completed form, supporting documents, and proof of travel and policy.
Keep copies of all correspondence, transport, and evacuation records for your claim.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for Tanzania
items.body_md:
Medical care in Tanzania is not free for tourists, and costs for hospital treatment or medical evacuation can be very expensive. Your travel insurance should cover local treatment and unexpected medical evacuation, including helicopter rescue if you plan outdoor activities such as hiking. Check that your policy’s evacuation limits and activity cover match your itinerary.

All visitors to Zanzibar (excluding residents) must have mandatory travel insurance for the duration of their stay up to 92 days, so confirm this requirement before you travel. In an emergency, call 112 for an ambulance and contact your insurer quickly if you are referred to a medical facility.

Before buying or using a policy, read the wording carefully and ask your insurer about cover for medical costs, evacuation, and any planned activities. Keep your insurance details and emergency contact numbers with you at all times.
claim_checklist: Call 112 and ask for an ambulance if needed.
Contact your insurer as soon as possible after you are referred to a medical facility.
Keep all medical bills, receipts, and reports.
Record details of the incident, including dates and names of facilities.
Ask the insurer for their next steps and required documentation.

items.title: Travel insurance guidance for the United States
items.body_md:
In the United States, health care is excellent but treatment costs are expensive, and foreign visitors without travel health insurance will normally have to pay out of pocket for all services. Emergency rooms must accept and treat emergencies regardless of ability to pay, but you will still be charged. Make sure your policy covers local medical treatment costs and unexpected medical evacuation.

If you are referred to a medical facility, contact your insurance or medical assistance company quickly. Keep your policy details and the insurer’s emergency contact number with you, along with accessible funds, because you may need to pay upfront. Note that Medicare has limited coverage outside the U.S., and travel insurance may not automatically include health cover, so check the policy wording and ask your insurer before you travel.
claim_checklist: Call 911 and ask for an ambulance if you need emergency medical help.
Contact your insurance or medical assistance company quickly if you are referred to a medical facility for treatment.
Keep all bills, receipts and medical documents from any treatment you receive.
Ask your insurer what evidence they require and follow their claim submission instructions.

items.title: Travel insurance for Uzbekistan: what to check
items.body_md:
Medical care in Uzbekistan is generally below the standards many travellers are used to, and outside Tashkent facilities are more limited, English-speaking staff are uncommon, and complex care may require transfer. Check that your policy covers private clinic and hospital costs, emergency treatment, and medical evacuation.

Emergency and trauma care may not be available or may not meet international standards, especially outside urban areas. Medical evacuation cover is particularly relevant for travel to places such as Khiva, Nukus or rural Karakalpakstan, and for adventure activities such as caving or remote travel where animal bites or injuries may need urgent care.

Keep your policy documents and the insurer's 24-hour assistance number with you. After any incident, contact your insurer as soon as possible and keep all receipts and reports. Always check the policy wording for exclusions, pre-existing conditions and activity cover, and ask the insurer if anything is unclear.
claim_checklist: Obtain a medical report or police report, if applicable, with dates, provider details and diagnosis or treatment.
Keep all receipts, invoices, prescriptions and discharge paperwork.
Contact your insurer's emergency assistance line as soon as you can.
Ask the insurer exactly which documents and forms are needed for your claim.
Submit the completed claim form and copies of all supporting documents by the deadline in your policy.
Keep copies of everything you send for your records.

items.title: Vietnam travel insurance: what to consider
items.body_md:
Travel insurance for Vietnam should cover emergency medical treatment and hospital stays, which can be expensive at private hospitals, as well as medical evacuation. This is especially important if you have a health condition or are pregnant, and you should confirm the destination can provide the healthcare you may need.

Dengue fever and malaria are present, so follow insect-bite precautions and be careful with food and water. Before travelling, consult a doctor or travel clinic about vaccinations and any anti-malarial medication; some treatments may not be safe during pregnancy. Cover for trip cancellation, lost or stolen belongings, and delays can reimburse prepaid flights, accommodation, and tours.

Keep your insurance policy details and 24/7 assistance number with you, along with proof of cover. After an incident, contact the assistance line as soon as possible, keep receipts and reports, and ask your insurer how to proceed. Always check your policy wording for exclusions and limits.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer or 24/7 emergency assistance number as soon as possible after the incident.
Keep receipts, medical reports, police reports and any travel provider paperwork.
Ask the insurer which claim forms and supporting documents are required.
Submit the claim within the deadline stated in your policy.
Keep copies of everything you send and note your claim reference.

items.title: Travel insurance essentials for South Africa
items.body_md:
South Africa has no reciprocal healthcare agreement with the UK, Australia, Canada or the US, so visitors must pay for all medical care. Private medical facilities are generally good, especially in urban areas and near game parks, but treatment, hospital stays and medical evacuation can be very expensive and may require payment or a deposit in advance.

Make sure your travel insurance covers emergency medical treatment, hospital admission, medical evacuation and repatriation. Evacuation cover is important if you travel outside major cities, where emergency services can be slow and air evacuation may be the only option.

Carry your insurance policy details and emergency assistance contact with you, along with funds or a payment card for upfront medical costs. If you take prescription medication, bring enough for your trip because some medicines may not be available locally. Check your policy wording and ask your insurer if you are unsure what is covered.
claim_checklist: Contact your insurer’s 24-hour emergency assistance line as soon as possible after a medical incident.
Go to a private medical facility if urgent care is needed and keep the insurer informed of your location.
Keep all receipts, invoices, medical reports and proof of any cash payments or deposits.
If evacuation or repatriation is advised, follow the insurer’s instructions rather than arranging it yourself.
Request copies of admission and discharge documents and prescriptions for your claim.
Submit your claim with the insurer’s required forms and supporting documents within the stated time limit.
